questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: Always give them the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross the street.
Only give them the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is this bicyclist signaling?

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead. A straight left arm means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: With a two-part seat belt system, wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing sign, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs and never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead turns at a sharp angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns at a sharp angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you to slow down for a sharp change in road direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is coming up ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to situations ahead. This sign warns you that a side road will intersect ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How far back should you drive?

options.text: Closer than you would behind a regular car.
Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have bigger blind spots. You need to follow farther behind a truck than you would behind a passenger car.

questions.question: Who can use handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
Anyone, but only if all other spaces are full.
People who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
questions.explanation: Handicap parking spaces are for people with disabilities only. You must have either the proper license plate or a designated hanging tag to park in these spaces.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you know?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip on gravel and dirt than on concrete and asphalt. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many accidents. Always drive at a safe speed within the legal limit and match the flow of traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light lets you proceed through the intersection. Yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and constantly pass them, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination faster and safer.
Increase your risk of a crash.
Help reduce traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a vehicle, your chance of a crash goes up.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Children on bikes may suddenly enter the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out and red lights flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep going when you think the children are done getting off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when a school bus has its stop arm extended and red lights flashing. Stay stopped until the stop arm goes up and the lights turn off.

questions.question: In a work zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.

questions.question: Which is true about changing lanes?

options.text: Only look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for right turns and left shoulder for left turns.
Two outside mirrors eliminate blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right turns and left shoulder for left turns.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: If a pedestrian crosses illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally. You must stop for them no matter where they cross.

questions.question: Before you stop at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.
Check your mirrors for nearby traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for nearby traffic.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before stopping. Be aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly to stop.

questions.question: Which of these is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic conditions and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If you see a solid yellow line next to your lane, you may not cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights
High beam headlights
Parking lights

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: In fog, always use low beams. High beams reflect off the fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating high-fat foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system. Eating and drinking cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower
Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed
questions.explanation: Never pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians crossing may be hidden from view. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: Before moving back to your original lane after passing, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
Flash your headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: When passing, check your rearview mirror for both headlights of the vehicle you passed. Only then is it safe to return to your original lane.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing
An orange background with black writing
A yellow background with blue writing

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: This sign warns of:

options.text: An intersection
A road curve
A right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: It is illegal to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone
Pass over a railroad crossing
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones or over railroad crossings. Also do not pass at street crossings, where solid yellow lines are next to your lane, on hills, in curves, near stopped pedestrians, or in work zones.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explanation: When turning left, always yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.
